scenario_name: No grab bar seen near the toilet
condition: (in_room(room='bathroom') AND present_for(class_name='toilet', seconds=60) AND NOT ever_seen(class_name='support_handle'))
next_best_action: Consider fitting a grab bar beside the toilet and inside the tub or shower.

capability_disclaimer: This reports how long a person has been visible in the bathroom. It cannot tell bathing from illness from a fall, and it is not fall detection.

scenario_name: Cord seen on the floor in a walkway
next_best_action: Coil or tape loose cords along the wall
capability_disclaimer: The system cannot tell a cord lying across the walking path from one running along the skirting board: there is no floor plane and no path model. Treat this as a prompt to look, not a confirmed hazard.

condition: (in_room(room='kitchen') AND present_for(class_name='stove', seconds=60) AND ever_seen(class_name='person') AND absent_for(class_name='person', seconds=900))
next_best_action: Ask someone to check the kitchen

scenario_name: Knife left out with nobody present
condition: (in_room(room='kitchen') AND present_for(class_name='knife', seconds=60) AND absent_for(class_name='person', seconds=600))
next_best_action: Put the knife away when convenient
Consider a pill organiser if packaging is often left out
capability_disclaimer: This is an observation of packaging position only. The system cannot tell whether any medication was taken, which medication it is, or when it is due.

scenario_name: Walking aid left away from the person
next_best_action: Check the walking stick is within easy reach
capability_disclaimer: The system sees where the walking stick is, not whether it is needed or being used. A stick resting in its usual place is not evidence of anything.

rejection_reason: No pose estimation, no keypoints, no floor plane and no motion model. A person box that becomes wide and low is someone bending, sitting on the floor, praying or exercising. This is the first capability every family will assume the product has, so the exclusion must also appear in the product surface, not only here.
No flame or heat state. `stove` is a physical object and is always detected. The legacy rule asserted this at risk_rules.yaml:54.
Requires a gas sensor. A camera cannot see LPG.

No pill count, no schedule, no drug identity and no speech recognition. Asking an unanswerable question invites a resolve-the-uncertainty second dose, which is a serious-harm pathway for narrow-therapeutic-index drugs common in this population. See SC-MED-001 for the honest replacement.
No fill level and no drinking event. Bottle presence is not fluid intake.
No pose, no vitals and no motion analysis.
`door` has no open/closed state and no threshold-crossing semantics.
Requires longitudinal ADL modelling far beyond object presence, and is a medical claim regardless of how it is worded.

No grip, no motion and no surface or edge classes. `knife` plus `person` is cooking, a preserved IADL; warning about it degrades the capacity it claims to protect. See SC-KIT-002 for the supportable form.
`face` yields no identity, and adding identity would be a deliberate step into biometric processing the project has committed against.

scenario_name: Nobody seen for an unusually long time
capability_disclaimer: Not seeing a person is not the same as nobody being there. This can equally mean the camera view is blocked or the person is out of frame, and it is never evidence of an emergency.
